title: Every pair can react while the final three-site construction is impossible
statement: A port(j,p) is accessible at retained-guide set F iff no simultaneous blocker H in B_(j,p) is contained in F. With three one-port sites and B_j={the other two}, either second reaction is accessible but every last reaction is blocked. Pairwise compatibility therefore does not imply serial completion. An obstruction-free second port at site2 makes a successful order exist.

body: A singleton footprint cannot contain a two-site blocking set, whereas the final retained pair equals the last site blocker. The example is exact under permanent monotone guide footprints, without imperfect bond chemistry. A release-aware state is(S,F), F subset S: choose an unfinished prerequisite-qualified site and an accessible port, mark it complete, and either retain its guide or pay one immediate safe release. Backward induction on unfinished sites proves that minimizing these transitions returns the minimum assumed release count. It gives existence with outcome-aware scheduling; it does not choose an actual unobserved reaction order. One release suffices for the symmetric triple; with the safe alternate port, complete0,1,2 without release. Cooperative blocking is unmeasured for the source-cited oxanine platform and does not contradict a pairwise theorem restricted to singleton blockers.
